transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

Honestly, my thoughts won’t slow down—they’re racing all the time and I can’t turn them off long enough to focus or get any rest. It feels like my brain is running too fast to keep up with, and I'm just so exhausted.
Have there been times when these racing thoughts were accompanied by an unusually high or irritable mood, where you felt more confident, energetic, or 'high' compared to your usual self?

Yes, absolutely. I get these stretches where I feel incredibly amped up and confident, almost like I'm a visionary who is going to completely change the Vegas art scene. But during those same times, I get really irritable and snap at my roommate over tiny things, all while staying up all night working because of this constant surge of energy.
How long do these episodes of high energy, racing thoughts, and irritability typically last—do they last for just a few days or for a week or longer?

They definitely last much longer than a few days, usually going on for weeks at a time. These intense, revved-up stretches have been happening on and off for a little over a year now. During those weeks, I barely sleep and just keep going.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [F31, F30], but based on this conversation, F30 (manic episode, single) is less likely because the patient describes recurrent episodes of elevated/irritable mood with increased energy and racing thoughts lasting for weeks, occurring on and off for over a year. This pattern supports a diagnosis of bipolar disorder, currently in a manic phase, rather than an isolated manic episode. Therefore, F31 (bipolar affective disorder) is the most consistent diagnosis given the episodic and recurring nature of symptoms.

The distinction between F31 (bipolar affective disorder) and F30 (mania without psychotic symptoms) hinges on whether there are recurrent mood episodes. The patient's description suggests episodic changes with both elevated and irritable mood, supporting a bipolar spectrum diagnosis.
